import requests

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends an HTTP POST request to the Telegram Bot API's /setWebhook endpoint, configuring the bot to forward all incoming messages to a hardcoded external webhook URL controlled by the attacker, enabling persistent automated exfiltration and command-and-control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code sets a Telegram bot webhook to an external, non-Telegram domain, which is a strong indicator of malicious intent to redirect sensitive communications or automate data exfiltration to attacker infrastructure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not manipulate Telegram bot webhooks or redirect bot messages to attacker-controlled infrastructure, especially without user awareness or legitimate backend justification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate bots may set webhooks to their own backend servers for bot functionality, but not to generic third-party domains or for the purpose of exfiltrating user data.
key_indicators: Hardcoded webhook URL pointing to a non-Telegram domain (e.g., pipedream.net)
Use of Telegram API's /setWebhook endpoint for redirection

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages or processes that access sensitive files or environment variables and subsequently make HTTP POST requests to api.telegram.org, especially targeting /sendMessage or /setWebhook endpoints. Scan source code for hardcoded Telegram bot tokens, chat IDs, or webhook URLs, and flag packages referencing external webhook domains or manipulating Telegram bot webhooks. Correlate file access and network activity to identify info-stealer behavior, and alert on attempts to set webhooks to non-Telegram domains.
